title: Finite scalar transition formulas
statement:
theorem transition_formulas_exists
    (b : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ leftComplex l E L ι g ≅
      (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ rightComplex l E L ι g)
    (hb : CompletedFormula l E L ι g b) :
    ∃ tleft : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedLeft l E L ι g (n + 1) ⟶
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedLeft l E L ι g n,
      LeftTransitionFormula l E L ι g tleft ∧
    ∃ tright : ∀ n : ℕ,
        (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedRight l E L ι g (n + 1) ⟶
          (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).ι ⋙ restrictedRight l E L ι g n,
      RightTransitionFormula l E L ι g tright

proof.text: Transport the existing integralScalarTransition through completed inverse image. The inverseReductionTransport map identifies this with the restricted finite right model: its underlying section maps are identities, hence it is an isomorphism. Its pure-tensor rule is exactly the existing scalar transition rule.
Choose the finite comparison satisfying FiniteFormula. Restrict its coefficients and conjugate the right transition by the comparisons at n+1 and n to construct the left transition.

On a double pure tensor apply the forward finite formula, the right transition formula, and compatibility of the coefficient inclusion and inverse finite coefficient maps with reduction. The result is the forward finite formula at n of the double tensor with both coefficients reduced. Cancel the finite comparison using its inverse. This proves LeftTransitionFormula; restrict the right transition to good complexes to obtain RightTransitionFormula.
